questions.q:
An unsafe query built by concatenation vs a parameterized one. What are the counts?
```python
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect(':memory:'); c.execute('create table u(n)'); c.executemany('insert into u values(?)',[('a',),('b',)])
v="x' OR '1'='1"
bad=c.execute("select count(*) from u where n='"+v+"'").fetchone()[0]
good=c.execute('select count(*) from u where n=?',(v,)).fetchone()[0]
print(bad,good)
```
questions.explain: Concatenation lets input change the query; parameters keep it data (demonstrated on a local in-memory DB). Verified by running it.

challenges.title: Turn a scan into an attack-surface report
challenges.prompt: Parse nmap grepable-style lines into {host: [(port, service, version)]} keeping only open ports, then print one line per host and a flagged line for each risky service (ftp, telnet, mysql, vnc) with remediation advice. Host: 10.10.10.9 ()  Ports: 443/open/tcp//https//nginx 1.25/, 445/closed/tcp//microsoft-ds///

"""

RISKY = {
    "ftp": "cleartext protocol: prefer SFTP and disable anonymous access",
    "telnet": "cleartext remote shell: replace with SSH",
    "mysql": "database exposed to the network: restrict by firewall",
    "vnc": "remote desktop exposed: tunnel via VPN / require strong auth",
}

def parse(scan):

    return {}

def report(hosts):
